subsystems.name: Soft actuator body
subsystems.role: the flexible structure that bends, extends or twists when pressurised, mimicking muscle.

subsystems.name: Fluid power and control
subsystems.role: supplies and precisely modulates the pressure that drives the actuator.

subsystems.name: Sensing and feedback
subsystems.role: measures position, force and contact so the surgeon or controller knows what the robot is doing.

subsystems.name: Stiffness modulation
subsystems.role: lets the device switch between rigid for insertion and soft for safe navigation.

subsystems.name: End effector
subsystems.role: interacts with tissue — grasping, cutting, suction or cautery.

subsystems.name: Control console and software
subsystems.role: maps the surgeon’s input to actuator motion and enforces safety limits.

buildSteps.title: Design the actuator
buildSteps.detail: Use computer models to simulate how elastomer chambers deform under pressure, and choose channel geometry for the desired motion.

buildSteps.title: Make moulds
buildSteps.detail: 3D-print or machine moulds for each elastomer layer, with features that will become internal channels.

buildSteps.title: Cast elastomer layers
buildSteps.detail: Pour liquid silicone or thermoplastic elastomer into the moulds and cure them at controlled temperature.

buildSteps.title: Add reinforcement
buildSteps.detail: Lay fibres or fabrics that constrain expansion in some directions, so the actuator bends or twists instead of just inflating.

buildSteps.title: Bond layers
buildSteps.detail: Assemble the layers with adhesive or thermal bonding to form sealed internal chambers.

buildSteps.title: Attach fluidic connectors
buildSteps.detail: Insert and seal tubing so pressurised air or fluid can enter and leave each chamber.

buildSteps.title: Embed sensors
buildSteps.detail: Place pressure and strain sensors in or on the soft body without stiffening it.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and test
buildSteps.detail: Connect the actuator to its control unit, test range of motion and force, and check for leaks.

buildSteps.title: Sterilise and package
buildSteps.detail: Clean, sterilise with a method compatible with the elastomer, and package for surgical use.

prerequisites.why: silicone and polyurethane are already used in short-term medical devices and can be moulded into soft shapes.
high-resolution, multi-material printing of soft robots is still developing, limiting complex monolithic designs.
precise, fast pressure control in a package small enough for surgery remains a challenge.
measuring deformation and force inside a soft structure without adding stiffness is difficult.
many elastomers withstand autoclave or gamma sterilisation, but each design must be validated.

pathway.milestone: prototypes tested in animals and cadavers for procedures such as cardiac ablation and endoscopy
pathway.unlocks: proof of safety and dexterity in real anatomy.

pathway.milestone: first clinical trials for specific procedures, for example transanal or single-incision surgery
pathway.unlocks: regulatory approval and early commercial use.

pathway.milestone: integration with real-time imaging (MRI, ultrasound) and haptic feedback
pathway.unlocks: the surgeon can feel and see what the soft robot touches.

pathway.milestone: semi-autonomous soft robots that navigate to a target and perform tasks
pathway.unlocks: reduced surgeon fatigue and access to deeper, delicate anatomy.
